written: Sun Oct 11 2026 03:10 EDT (by `date`), stage S3, AFTER the S1 run (38119008371), the S2 run (38119607308) and the investigation run (38119645255) existed, and BEFORE the first S3 matrix run of .github/workflows/measure.yml; no S3 number existed when this file was committed
changelog: v2 (stage S3). Written after S1 and S2 results existed, so the new rules below are NOT pre-registered in the sense criteria.json (v1) was: they were written knowing those numbers. Why they exist: the investigation (investigate/FINDINGS.md) found that the FAST/NONE ratio of the forward kernel k02_add_fwd (1.6x on EPYC 7763 and 9V74, 0.98x on 9V45, 1.075x at L1 on the Xeon 8573C of S2) comes from where the hot loop lands: under FAST clang picks interleave 1 and the 31-byte SIMD loop straddles a 64-byte boundary. With -falign-loops=64 the FAST/NONE ratio became 0.82 to 1.0 on all three CPUs. A byte-identical A/A cannot see this kind of noise, and the same binary behaves differently on different CPU models.

What v2 adds: (1) a second NONE/FAST pair built with -falign-loops=64 for every kernel and program (the 'loops aligned' column beside 'as compiled'); (2) a layout A/A (NONE against NONE built with -falign-loops=64); (3) each build's loop placement recorded; (4) one verdict per runner CPU model, and a page-level line that is a map only when every CPU model with a usable A/A agrees.

What v2 does not change: every rule and threshold of criteria.json (v1) is copied below unchanged in 'design', 'classes_from_remarks' and 'verdict'. criteria.json itself stays as the record, and every S3 results.json also carries 'verdict_v1': the v1 rules applied to its as-compiled column, so the pre-registered answer stays visible beside the v2 one.

Rule for changes, as in v1: no threshold here is changed, loosened or added after a result from the S3 harness exists. If one looks unfair, the result is reported against it as written and the objection is written beside it.
supersedes: criteria.json (v1) as the rule that decides results.json 'verdict' for runs that name this file in run.criteria_file; criteria.json keeps deciding 'verdict_v1' and every earlier run
rule_for_changes: No threshold in this file is changed, loosened or added after a result from the S3 harness exists.

kernels.k01_sum_fwd: s += a[i], i up, int64 accumulator
kernels.k06_gather: c[i] = a[idx[i]], idx a fixed-seed permutation of 0..n-1
kernels.k08_matmul: d x d, order i-k-j, c[i*d+j] += a[i*d+k] * b[k*d+j], inputs masked to 0..3 so no int32 overflows

design.element_type: int32_t in std::vector, accessed through operator[]; each kernel a noinline function kern_<id>
design.size_classes: working set counts every array of the kernel; L1 = half of L1d, L2 = half of L2, RAM = four times the last-level cache capped at 256 MiB; cache sizes from /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/cache

skipped_cells.k08_matmul.RAM: not measured: at a RAM-sized working set one i-k-j call streams all of b once per row, an estimated 10 s or more per call and over 10 minutes per cell; RAM cells are not in N or the limits

builds.novec: the NONE flags plus -fno-vectorize (timing positive control)
builds.aa: the NONE binary of the A/A kernel copied to a second path; the run aborts if the two sha256 differ

design.aa_pair: k02_add_fwd at the L1 size, NONE against its byte-identical copy, timed like every other pair, in every run

timing.order: ABBA repeated (A B B A A B B A ...), one process per repetition, pinned with taskset -c to one CPU
timing.clock: clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC) inside the binary around the timed loop; process start, input fill and one warm-up call excluded
timing.inner_iterations: calibrated once per cell on the NONE build to about 75 ms per process, reused unchanged for every build of that cell
timing.interval: percentile bootstrap, 10000 resamples of each side independently, seed 20261011, 95 %, harness/stats.py

design.novec_pairs: timed only for kernels vectorized in NONE (from the remarks), at the in-cache sizes
design.cachegrind: valgrind --tool=cachegrind --cache-sim=no at the L1 size, 20 inner iterations; Ir attributed to kern_<id> divided by the number of calls (inner iterations plus one warm-up); instructions, not time

classes_from_remarks.on_axis: a kernel whose loop clang reports as vectorized in the NONE build
classes_from_remarks.kept: on_axis and vectorized in FAST: the forward class (negative control)
classes_from_remarks.lost: on_axis and not vectorized in FAST: the class that pays
classes_from_remarks.off_axis: not vectorized in NONE: reported, not used for N, the forward limit or the controls

verdict.ram_cells: reported, never in N, the forward limit, the lost minimum or the positive control
verdict.positive_control_seen: at least one in-cache cell of an on_axis kernel has a NOVEC/NONE ratio with ci95_lo > 1 + aa_half_width_pct / 100
order: INCONCLUSIVE (A/A control) if the A/A half-width exceeds aa_half_width_max_pct
INCONCLUSIVE (checksum) if any measured cell has checksum_match false
INCONCLUSIVE (positive control) if the positive control is not seen
INCONCLUSIVE (negative control) if no kernel is in the kept class

MAP if every in-cache cell of a kept kernel has ratio <= forward_point_max_ratio AND ci95_hi <= the forward ci_hi limit, AND every in-cache cell of a lost kernel has ci95_lo >= lost_ci_lo_min_ratio, AND at least one kernel is in the lost class
HOLDS_EVERYWHERE if no in-cache cell of an on_axis kernel has ci95_lo above the forward ci_hi limit (X = the largest ci95_hi over those cells, as a percent above 1, floored at 0)
verdict.N: median of ratio over the in-cache cells of the lost kernels, with min and max; RAM cells not in N
verdict.forward_limit_pct: the forward ci_hi limit as a percent: max(2.0, 2 * aa_half_width_pct)

v2.scope: one results.json = one Actions job = one runner; its verdict is the verdict for that runner's CPU model (run.runner.cpu_model)

pairs_added.aligned: fast_a64 against none_a64 for every cell and program, the same n and inner iterations as the as-compiled pair, ABBA, reps_per_side per side; stored in the cell's (program's) 'aligned' key
pairs_added.layout_aa: none against none_a64 (the same source and mode, only the loop alignment differs) for every kernel at the in-cache sizes and for every program; stored in controls.layout_aa

v2.placement_record: for every kernel build (none, fast, novec, none_a64, fast_a64): each loop in kern_<id> with start, bytes, start_mod64, crosses64, windows64, extra_window, simd, innermost (harness/placement.py); for programs a whole-binary count
v2.layout_aa_half_width: the largest half_width_pct among the designated layout A/A pairs present in the run

columns.as_compiled: the cell's ratio and ci95 (the v1 pair, unchanged)

v2.headline_column: aligned: the forward rule, N and X are read from the loops-aligned pair; the as-compiled pair is shown beside it (verdict.n_as_compiled, and both columns in the lost rule)
v2.placement_sensitive: a kept-class (forward) in-cache cell whose two ratios disagree by more than the layout A/A half-width: 100 * |ratio - aligned.ratio| > layout_aa_half_width_pct. It is excluded from the forward rule and from X, and listed in verdict.placement_sensitive and in the line
v2.off_axis_reading: an off-axis in-cache cell (not vectorized in NONE, e.g. k06_gather, k07_hist) is described as paying for the check only when ci95_lo is above the forward ci_hi limit in BOTH columns; listed in verdict.off_axis, never in N, X or the form
order: INCONCLUSIVE (A/A control) if the byte-identical A/A half-width exceeds aa_half_width_max_pct (2 %), as in v1
INCONCLUSIVE (checksum) if any cell has a NONE/FAST checksum mismatch in either column
INCONCLUSIVE (build control) if a cell lacks the aligned pair, or the aligned builds' remarks disagree with the as-compiled builds' vectorized flags
INCONCLUSIVE (layout control) if no designated layout A/A pair is present

MAP if at least one forward in-cache cell is left after the placement-sensitive exclusions, every such cell passes the v1 forward rule (ratio <= forward_point_max_ratio AND ci95_hi <= the forward ci_hi limit) on its aligned pair, every in-cache cell of a lost kernel has ci95_lo >= lost_ci_lo_min_ratio in BOTH columns, and at least one kernel is in the lost class

HOLDS_EVERYWHERE if no in-cache cell of an on_axis kernel, placement-sensitive cells excluded, has ci95_lo above the forward ci_hi limit in either column (X = the largest ci95_hi of those cells in either column, as a percent above 1, floored at 0)
v2.N: median of aligned.ratio over the in-cache cells of the lost kernels, with min and max; the same over the as-compiled ratios is verdict.n_as_compiled
v2.forward_limit_pct: as in v1: max(2.0, 2 * the byte-identical A/A half_width_pct)
v2.line: the v1 wording, prefixed with 'On <cpu_model>: ', naming the aligned column, and followed by the placement-sensitive cells with both ratios when there are any

page_level.input: every results.json of one workflow run (one per matrix job), grouped by run.runner.cpu_model; harness/combine.py writes combined.json
page_level.usable: a results file whose byte-identical A/A half-width is at most aa_half_width_max_pct
page_level.cpu_form: the form of the CPU model's usable files when they all agree; inconclusive when they disagree; a CPU model with no usable file is listed as excluded (A/A) and does not vote
page_level.form: map only if at least one CPU model is usable and every usable CPU model's form is map; holds_everywhere only if every usable CPU model's form is holds_everywhere; otherwise inconclusive, and the line names which CPU model differs and why
page_level.N: median of aligned.ratio over the lost kernels' in-cache cells pooled across the usable files that are map, with min and max; X = the largest X of those files
